submission.natural_language_explanation: L9/N1018+ detects the causative/resultative frame of 'make': it fires on the verb 'make' in any inflection ('makes', 'make', 'made', 'making') when that verb takes a (pro)noun object plus a predicative complement that states the object's resulting property, state or experience - an adjective ('makes it convenient', 'makes the Avenues unique', 'makes it mandatory', 'make it all the more interesting'), a mental-state or perception verb ('made me wonder', 'make you feel', 'makes it seem so far away', 'make your food taste sweet'), or 'to be' - or, with no separate complement, in the two degree idioms 'make (a lot of / little / no) sense' and 'make (little / no / big) difference'. It is the frame, not the word form and not the word: all four inflections reach near the pole's maximum of 2.69 in this frame (the 20 top peaks contain 7 ' makes', 6 ' make' and 1 ' made', and ' make' has more firing instances in absolute terms than ' makes' despite its lower mean), whereas the same token stays near zero in physical creation ('make a cake', 'made him dinner', 'makes cars in three factories'), in light-verb action nouns ('make a decision', 'make a call', 'make a mistake'), and in fixed, phrasal or commercial uses ('make money', 'make it to the party', 'make up', 'the make and model'), and near-synonymous causatives do not fire ('render it mandatory', 'deem X Y', 'regard X as Y' sit at 0.24-0.40 mean, 9-15% of max). The peak sits on 'make' itself and spills onto the object and degree words (' little', ' a', ' it', ' you'), 29% of input attribution lies more than 16 tokens back (the frame's subject), and with Jacobian kurtosis 3.12 and 40% lens overlap the output promotes no coherent next-token set, so this is retrospective frame detection rather than lookahead. Known residue this claim does not cover: about 30% of the top peaks (both ' El' peaks are 'Elmore', both ' j' peaks are 'jpg'/'jellies', plus ' of' in 'Idylls of the King' and ' to' in 'device to enhance') look like a separate weak sensitivity to BPE word-onset fragments in name, URL and formatting contexts (the confound list's '@', ' www', 'EL', ' u'), and should be probed separately.

CHAIR NGUYEN: Good evening, everyone. This is the regular meeting of the parks and recreation board for the ninth of May. We have three items on the agenda, and I would ask speakers to keep their remarks to two minutes so we can get through all of them.

ITEM ONE: MINUTES. The minutes of the April meeting were circulated last week. Hearing no corrections, they stand approved.

ITEM TWO: AQUATIC CENTER REPAIRS. Director Alvarez, would you walk us through the schedule?

DIRECTOR ALVAREZ: Thank you. The replacement pump arrived on Friday, but the contractor found corrosion in the intake line that was not visible during the winter inspection. That line has to be cut out and refabricated before the new pump can be tied in. The fabricator has quoted eight working days from receipt of the drawings, and the drawings went out this morning. Until the line is back in service, we will keep the shallow end closed and run the lap lanes on a reduced schedule.

RESIDENT OKAFOR: Eight days seems long. Is there any way to rent a temporary pump?

DIRECTOR ALVAREZ: We looked into it. A rental unit of the right capacity is available from a supplier in Stockton, but the tie-in still requires the same line work, so it would not save us any time. It would also cost about eleven thousand dollars for the month.

CHAIR NGUYEN: And the lap lanes?

DIRECTOR ALVAREZ: We can run four lanes instead of six during the mornings, which makes the facility far less useful to the swim clubs that rent lanes from us on weekday mornings. The clubs have been very patient, but two of them have asked about moving their practices to the high school pool for the rest of the month. I would rather not lose them.

RESIDENT BAPTISTE: My daughter is on one of those teams. The schedule changes every week and we plan around it, but the communication has been poor. The sign on the door still shows the old hours.

DIRECTOR ALVAREZ: That is fair. We will post updated hours tonight and send a note to each club.

RESIDENT OKAFOR: What about the scaffolding by the main doors? The crew left it up over the weekend and the wind knocked a panel into the planting bed.

DIRECTOR ALVAREZ: I saw that this morning. The panel is back in place and the bed will be replanted on Thursday. In the meantime the scaffolding makes the entrance look like a construction site, and I have asked the crew to screen it with netting.

CHAIR NGUYEN: Any further comments on item two? Hearing none, we will take the repair schedule as presented and revisit it at the June meeting. Moving to item three, the summer camp fee schedule.
